sentences.text: This dinosaur grew to a length of approximately 8.3 meters and a mass of 2.5 tonnes.
Its specific name spinorhinus translates to 'with a nose spine,' referencing the unique crest on its snout.
Scientists propose that the hollow tube inside this crest reduced weight while keeping the structure strong.

Fossils were uncovered in 1950 at Hsikou near Chingkangkou in Laiyang, Shandong, China. Chinese paleontologist C. C. Young formally described the species in 1958. The genus name honors the city of Qingdao, which was once spelled Tsintao in Latin.
It possessed a duck-bill snout and powerful teeth designed for chewing plants.
The animal likely breathed air through paired openings located behind the upper beak.
While it usually walked on four legs, it could stand upright on its hind legs to spot predators or escape them.
Evidence suggests this animal traveled and lived in groups, similar to other hadrosaurs.
Tsintaosaurus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae and the parent group Lambeosaurinae. It may form a clade within Lambeosaurinae alongside the European genera Pararhabdodon and Koutalisaurus.
In 1990, researchers Weishampel and Horner suggested the crest was actually a distorted broken nasal bone rather than a real structure.
However, in 1993, Eric Buffetaut and colleagues concluded after renewed investigation that the crest was neither distorted nor a restoration product.
A 2013 study by Prieto-Márquez and Wagner concluded that the crest was the rear part of a larger cranial structure extending from the snout tip.

Researchers assumed Tsintaosaurus had a similar nasal arrangement to its lambeosaurine relatives, suggesting air entered the skull through paired pseudonarinas, or 'false nasal pits,' behind the upper beak upon inhalation. Based on this, researchers concluded that airflow was completely separated and that the central common chamber was likely divided into right and left sections by a cartilaginous septum.
